title: Obsidian round 2: annotate/override loop, batch extract, dogfood-2
description:
Round 2 of the Obsidian layer. Three deliverables:

1. ANNOTATE/OVERRIDE LOOP: `memsub vault apply --vault DIR` reads human edits
   back into the store. Correction (body text edit) supersedes with a new
   human-verified episode (ranks above agent-inferred per observed-beats-inferred
   rule). Rejection (verdict: reject) forgets the memory. Confirm (verdict: confirm)
   marks human-confirmed, protected from decay. Human-edit detection via a
   content_hash stored in frontmatter at sync time, compared at apply time.
   Never touches notes sync itself would still produce unchanged.

2. BATCH EXTRACT: `memsub extract` takes multiple files / glob patterns, with
   a --min-turns filter (default filters single-shot automation dumps).

3. DOGFOOD-2: batch extract over a real sample of ~/.claude/projects/ with
   ollama qwen3:8b, consolidate, sync to the SAME vault (~/memsub-vault).
   Exercise annotate end to end: >=1 correction, >=1 rejection, >=1 confirm,
   with apply run and store/audit/next-sync all verified to reflect it.

ACCEPTANCE CHECKS (pre-registered before build):
- [ ] pytest green at every commit (uv venv, .venv/bin/python -m pytest)
- [ ] vault.py: content_hash written in frontmatter at sync time
- [ ] vault.py: apply_vault() implements correction/reject/confirm with
      documented precedence (reject > correction > confirm > no-op)
- [ ] consolidate.py: decay phase skips episodes with a "confirmed" event
- [ ] round-trip test: sync -> apply (no edits) -> 0 corrections/rejections/
      confirmations, all notes report unchanged/skipped-inactive as appropriate
- [ ] round-trip test: sync -> edit -> apply -> sync again converges, no
      spurious diffs (idempotent second apply does not re-fire)
- [ ] CLI: `memsub vault apply --db DB --vault DIR` wired, tested
- [ ] CLI: `memsub extract` accepts multiple files/globs, --min-turns flag
      with sensible default, existing single-file tests still pass
- [ ] docs/obsidian-layer.md updated: annotate semantics, what apply does
      and does not do
- [ ] docs/dogfood-2-2026-07-12.md written: scale, timings, 3 real annotate
      cases with honest before/after, UX friction
- [ ] real dogfood run against ~/memsub-vault (outside git) using ollama
      qwen3:8b backend, no transcript/vault content committed to repo
- [ ] no em dash characters in any file written
- [ ] no fabricated numbers; all counts/timings from actual runs
- [ ] does NOT build staging-vault or shared-notes ideas (out of scope)

title: Obsidian vault export layer + dogfood on real Claude Code transcripts
description: Build 'memsub vault sync --vault PATH [--namespace NS]': exports the episodic store to a plain-markdown Obsidian-compatible vault (one note per memory, YAML frontmatter, provenance section, wiki-links for shared entities and supersede chains, per-namespace index notes, top-level MOC). Idempotent/re-runnable: stable id-based filenames, update changed notes, remove notes for deleted memories. Then dogfood: run memsub extract -> consolidate -> vault sync over Rustom's real Claude Code transcripts at ~/.claude/projects/ into ~/memsub-vault (outside any git repo). design: Reuse Episode/EpisodicStore schema as-is, no schema changes. New file memsub/vault.py: sync_vault(store, vault_path, namespace=None) -> VaultSyncResult. Entity extraction reuses the same naive capitalized-word regex idea as memsub/sleep.py's _extract_entities for shared-entity links, kept dependency-free like the rest of the repo. Obsidian layer idea 3: staging/approve-before-apply for consolidate
description:
Second-layer idea #3 from docs/obsidian-layer.md, not built in this round
(shipped idea #1 -- human notes promotion, memsub vault promote -- instead;
see commit 20fa3b6 and docs/obsidian-layer.md's Second-layer ideas section).

GOAL: an opt-in --stage flag on `memsub consolidate` so destructive actions
(supersede, forget) are written as pending proposals into the vault instead
of applied immediately. `memsub vault apply` then executes accepted
proposals and drops rejected ones. Default consolidate behavior (no flag)
must stay exactly as it is today.

WHY NOT BUILT THIS ROUND: assessed as too large to land cleanly with tests
alongside idea #1 in the same pass. It needs a real state machine across
two commands (consolidate --stage, vault apply), not just a new function:

DESIGN SKETCH:
1. consolidate(..., dry_run=True) already computes Actions (supersede/
   forget) without applying them -- reuse that path for --stage instead of
   adding new action-computation logic.
2. New function stage_actions(actions, vault_path, namespace) writes one
   proposal note per action into <vault>/staging/, e.g.
   staging/<namespace>/<action>--<episode_id8>.md, frontmatter: id (the
   episode this action targets), action ("supersede"|"forget"), reason,
   detail (by/similarity/judge_model/value/age_days/retrieved_count as
   applicable), status: pending. No verdict field yet -- human sets it.
3. Idempotency: re-running --stage must not write duplicate proposals for
   an action that's already staged-and-pending for the same episode+action.
   Check for an existing staging note with matching id+action+status:pending
   before writing a new one. Also must not re-stage an action whose episode
   is no longer active (already resolved by a prior apply run or a
   non-staged consolidate).
4. vault apply, in addition to its existing memory-note scan, scans
   staging/ for proposal notes. A note is read via the SAME frontmatter
   parsing regexes already in vault.py (FRONTMATTER_RE, _parse_frontmatter)
   -- do not fork new parsing logic. Verdict semantics on a staging note:
   - verdict: accept -> apply the action for real (log the "superseded" or
     "forgotten" event on the target episode, exactly what non-staged
     consolidate would have logged), then mark the staging note resolved
     (e.g. rewrite status: applied, or delete it -- pick one, be consistent
     with how apply already treats resolved memory notes).
   - verdict: reject -> drop it: mark status: rejected (or delete), do NOT
     touch the target episode.
   - no verdict (still pending) -> skip, leave as is.
   This is the "reject > correction > confirm" precedence idea mentioned in
   the original task spec, generalized to accept/reject on proposals rather
   than the memory-note verdict vocabulary; it isn't a literal reuse of
   apply's three-branch memory logic since proposals aren't episode edits,
   but it should reuse the same "read frontmatter, act on verdict, record
   outcome in VaultApplyResult.detail" shape apply already has, not a
   parallel bespoke system.
5. VaultApplyResult needs new counters (e.g. staged_applied,
   staged_rejected) or a decision to fold into existing corrected/
   rejected/confirmed counters -- needs a call, do not silently reuse
   existing counters if the semantics differ enough to confuse a reader of
   `memsub vault apply`'s summary line.
6. Test surface required before this can land: --stage computes but does
   not apply (store unchanged, actions appear in staging/); apply accept
   applies exactly the staged action; apply reject drops without touching
   the episode; re-running --stage after a prior stage is idempotent
   (no duplicate proposals); a staged-but-still-pending proposal is
   inert across repeated apply runs; default consolidate (no --stage) is
   byte-for-byte unchanged in behavior (regression guard against every
   existing consolidate test).

Read docs/obsidian-layer.md's "Second-layer ideas" section (idea #3) and
the "Annotate/override loop" section (precedence machinery to generalize
from) before starting.
close_reason: Shipped in commit 803c3ba: consolidate --stage writes pending proposals into vault/staging, vault apply executes accept/drops reject, idempotent re-staging, staged_applied/staged_rejected counters, regression guard. 9 new tests.
